rules.title: California Civil Code Section 1950.6 (tenant screening fees)
rules.requirement: Landlords may charge a screening fee capped annually, must give a receipt, itemization, copy of the credit report and refund unused portions, and may not charge if no unit is available. Landlords must use a reusable screening report if the tenant provides one.
rules.status_basis: Statute in the California Civil Code, described on the Berkeley Rent Board page; the 2026 fee figure is only an annual announcement.

coverage.summary: Applies to landlords screening prospective tenants of residential rentals.

rules.quoted_span: The landlord cannot charge a prospective tenant a screening fee if no rental unit is actually available.

rules.title: Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.78 (Tenant Screening and Application Fees)
rules.requirement: Owners who charge a credit-report/application processing fee must give a clear tenant screening fee rights statement and the state fee cap before receiving the fee. Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to remove or add a roommate. The chapter applies to all residential rental agreements despite contrary lease terms.
rules.status_basis: Codified in Berkeley Municipal Code Chapter 13.78.

coverage.summary: Applies to all residential rental property in Berkeley.

rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
